review_scope: Registered-source review of Sharp adaptive and pathwise stable similarity testing for scalar ergodic diffusions by Johannes Brutsche and Angelika Rohde. The verified local source is arXiv:2203.13776v3, dated 16 April 2024, 153 pages. Main text and references end on page 31. Only the separately titled supplement heading on page 32 was inspected, in a crop ending at y=180; no supplement body was used.
inventory: All ten actual Theorems are present: 3.1 on page 9, 4.1 on page 12, 5.1 on page 15, 5.2 and 5.3 on page 16, 5.4 on page 17, 6.1 on page 19, 6.3 on page 20, 6.5 on page 21 and 7.1 on page 23. Each complete statement fits on its recorded page and was compared with the rendered page. Small-caps heading enumeration covers all 31 main-text pages and excludes three ordinary-font mentions, including the external Theorem 1.16. Main-text Lemmas, Propositions and Remarks are not added to the theorem count.
original_statements: Theorem 3.1 retains continuous signed bounded-variation kernels with norm at most one, both empirical scale definitions including the squared interval indicator, asymptotic tightness under the stationary reference law and both the ratio convention and complete Upsilon formula.

Theorem 4.1 retains nonnegative kernels, the tightened reference-drift class, uniform limsup over the composite null, the complete two Gaussian suprema U1 and U2, both boundary densities and normalizers and the additive 4 sqrt(A eta/sigma^2) term. The common W is not replaced by independent drivers.

Theorem 5.1 retains arbitrary uniformly level tests, the full epsilon sequence conditions, weighted separation, the below-boundary minus-epsilon threshold and the compact interior J. Theorem 5.2 retains positive eta, its stronger unit-norm kernel condition, the above-boundary plus-epsilon threshold and its explicit beta<=1 optimal-kernel and sharp-constant clause.

Theorem 5.3 retains both rate adaptivity and sharp-L adaptivity. Its first outer infimum literally uses (b,L), and its sharp clause does not restate K=K_beta. Theorem 5.4 retains the original minus-epsilon threshold in its power-one conclusion and the reference to the simple test (3.6). These printed discrepancies are documented separately, without changing the statements.

Theorem 6.1 is the complete deterministic continuity assertion on D_A,T. Theorem 6.3 retains the conditional uniform probability limit and both orders of the iterated liminf for the domain event. Theorem 6.5 retains fixed x0, the time-dependent Hurst neighborhood, the order limsup/sup-H/sup-tests/inf-alternatives, the alpha+epsilon bound and the complete uniform size restriction on arbitrary tests.

Theorem 7.1 retains its inline Gaussian Z_b, both sigma definitions, S_b and uniform convergence over the full drift class. Its Brownian driver is indexed by space and is distinct from the observation-time driver. The following metric explanation on page 24 remains separate from the theorem statement.
source_passages: All 38 original member passages and nine auxiliary passages were compared with their main-text source. The scalar observation model, local Lipschitz drift class, growth and inward-drift bounds, normalized invariant density and signed integration convention agree with page 6. The invariant density can be a deterministic weight without a stationary observation law.

The pointwise norm and simple testing hypotheses on page 7, localized kernel without a 1/h multiplier, standardized score with its zero-denominator convention and rational location-bandwidth domain on page 8, empirical scales, correction, global statistic, finite-time quantile and strict rejection rule on page 9 remain distinct source entries.

The composite null and alternative, tolerance adjustment, similarity statistic, both limiting Gaussian statistics, limiting quantile and strict similarity rejection rule match pages 10-13. Minimum quantiles, non-strict CDF inequalities and strict test inequalities are preserved.

The weighted distance definition on page 13 and its following supremum formula on page 14 are both saved. The latter omits a positive part; no correction is inserted. The Holder definition uses a maximal integer strictly smaller than beta and quantifies over k while displaying only the highest derivative. Separation rate, sharp constant and optimal recovery problem remain separate. The explicit recovery kernel is restricted to beta<=1.

The signed, nonnegative, exact-unit-norm and additionally C1 kernel restrictions are not merged. The pathwise integral functional, domain of paths visiting both endpoints and extended score match page 18. The restricted bandwidth set and extended statistic match page 19, including the printed X in its f-dependent Lambda term.

The fractional Gaussian covariance, common Volterra representation and fixed-initial-value coupled solution notation match pages 19-20. The cross-H coupling is additional structure, not determined by the covariance. Global Lipschitz drift context is kept separate from the displayed domains in Theorem 6.5.

The metric description on page 24 and closed-unit-ball terminology on page 25 are retained. They defer the exact norm convention to the excluded supplement. The Section 7 proof processes and Proposition 7.3 are not added as dependencies of the theorem statements.
dependency_review: All 76 direct uses, 160 related connections and 38 local dependency lists were checked against the statement-resolution paths. The deterministic continuity theorem does not inherit a diffusion experiment. Fractional fixed-start theorems do not inherit stationary P_b. Arbitrary-test lower bounds do not depend on the proposed statistic, calibration or its kernel restrictions. The full-class Gaussian limit does not inherit the similarity-null restriction. Optimal recovery enters lower bounds through c_*, while only explicit kernel choices create direct optimal-kernel edges. Definitions bound inline remain preserved, without importing their proof arguments.
names_and_highlights: Every title uses source-backed natural-language wording. Assumptions, kernel conditions, theorem excerpts and neutral source passages retain their original types and source labels. Selectors identify each original passage or label and occur only there or in a related same-paper theorem. All 160 explanations follow actual paper-local paths. Rendered equations and source font checks distinguish script function/index/Holder classes from plain italic hypotheses, path domains and test statistics.
source_limitations: All 32 source notes and five excluded-reference records are retained. In particular, Appendix B h_min(T), Appendix I coupling kernel K_H and Appendix F.1 metric normalization remain unresolved. Appendix D local-Lipschitz wording and the fixed-point extensions in Remarks H.6/H.7 were not read. Other preserved issues include tightened drift-class parameter compatibility, zero kernels and undefined logarithmic expressions, distance positive-part omission, smoothness-index mismatch, the Theorem 5.4 minus sign, general optimal-kernel support, X/f mismatch, and the inherited variables and drift-domain ambiguity in Theorem 6.5. This review certifies source transcription and dependency accounting, not proofs or equivalence to final journal typesetting.
changes: No census-content correction was needed. All six content JSON files and the historical audit remain unchanged. Earlier scripts are archived. The per-paper rebuild now uses the verified fixed local PDF and reproduces all six content artifacts in an empty directory, without old temporary-file dependencies or creating new source-review approval.
validation: The independent inventory and census validators pass. All six regenerated files match the saved bytes. Additional checks cover source identity and version, title/authors/date, page count, all fresh main-text text pages, actual theorem headings, complete inventory handoff, source bounds, local/direct/recursive dependencies, source kinds, names, highlight selectors, mathematical delimiters, control characters and historical artifact hashes.
